snippet.title: Creed Movies Behind the Scenes
snippet.description:
With the release of Creed III, the epic Creed tale is officially a trilogy. It’s wild to think that after so many years of Rocky movies, there are still so many stories to tell from that universe. And the tales of Adonis Creed have definitely taken on a life of their own. You really don’t have to know anything about the Rocky movies to enjoy these flicks. And a big part of that is how much care and professionalism they put into making them. If you’re film obsessed like we are, then you know that the best way to find out about what went into making blockbusters like Creed, Creed II, and Creed III is to check out behind the scenes footage. Fortunately for all of us, they’ve released a bunch of BTS footage that we were able to dive into. In this video, we’re taking a look at all of the cool stuff we found while about the Creed movies from the behind the scenes action. We talk about how the most recent one features a first time director who we’ll call Michael B. Jordan. Ever heard of him? Yeah, the dude can basically do everything. And how they used IMAX cameras for Creed III, so you can see every bead of sweat dripping off these jacked boxers. We go over some of the many ways that the OG star, Sylvester Stallone contributed to the shoots. You’ll be able to watch as he guides the directors (Michael, Ryan Coogler, and Steven Caple Jr.), the actors, and the crew, showing them little tricks of the trade for making an epic boxing flick. We also get to see how much goofing around these actors and directors did, which is pretty cool when you think about what an intense and serious story they are telling with each movie. And much more! So check out this video, as we check out BTS footage from the Creed movies!

snippet.title: Inside the Series Dear Edward
snippet.description:
I went behind the scenes of Dear Edward so you didn’t have to! I found out that the role of Dee Dee was specifically written with Connie Britton in mind and Taylor Schilling was an incredible co-star and friend to her Colin O’Brien. Colin was working through some really tough emotions with this being his first leading role and all – on top of the fact that he recently lost his grandfather to Covid. He confided in Taylor and the two of them created a beautiful friendship as she helped him work through everything with playful banter and breathing exercises. The writer and creator of the series, Jason Katims, was so moved by the work everyone was doing on set that he was constantly finding himself crying in the editing room – much to his own embarrassment. Something else that was pretty spectacular – and a little intense – about the show was the grief group. The director of the episode, Allison Liddi-Brown, set the scene for all of the actors to really treat it like one. Everyone used their own grief and experiences in the scene and worked through real-life issues! It was truly a therapeutic moment on set. There are also quite a few narrative differences from the book to the show which is due to how character driven the writing is – which also opens it up to more seasons in the future. What do you think? Are you excited to see how Dear Edward plays out? Let us know in the comments!

Who didn’t love the DC and Warner Bros. Shazam. After DECADES of waiting, the original Captain Marvel, now called Shazam, finally arrived on the big screen in hilarious style. It’s a true classic that was lucky to actually finish. That’s because filming this movie was straight-up chaos. Not that the actors didn’t get along, mind you, but that they got along a little too well. Filming for this movie included constant joking around, pranks, and improvised scenes that made for a hilarious finished product, but likely a challenging shoot to get everyone to be serious long enough to film the actual movie. 

As far as getting serious is concerned, there was one area in which Zachary Levi was able to fully commit. That was in getting that legendary Shazam body he had through hours of working out and eating the blandest, healthiest food he could find. It’s a truly amazing sacrifice that not many could take. Especially when combined with the frigid temperatures of Toronto in winter that they had to contend with. It was no easy gig. You’ve also gotta consider how terrifying it is to work with Mark Strong. Sure, he seems like a nice guy, but he’s a terrifying presence to work with.

So what was it like behind the scenes of a movie like Shazam? Only one way to find out right now!

snippet.title: Tragic Accidents That Happened On Set
snippet.description:
BANG! A film set that was supposed to be a normal day of shooting suddenly turns everyone’s lives upside down. A gun that was supposed to be loaded with a blank was actually loaded with a live round on accident. Alec Baldwin, who wasn’s supposed to aim the gun at a person had accidentally fired at a coworker. A life was lost. The production was permanently damaged. A lawsuit emerged, dragging everyone involved into serious litigation. This was the story behind Rust, what was supposed to be a fun western throwback.

After Rust showed just how dangerous film sets can be a lot of attention has been drawn to similar on-set accidents that have happened for years. This includes a string of dangerous motorcycle stunts, such as those in Black Panther: Wakanda Forever or Maze Runner: The Death Cure. Then there’s the infamous parting of Quentin Tarantino and Uma Thurman over a stunt gone wrong in Kill Bill Vol. 2. No one should ever ignore the concerns of someone as cool as Uma Thurman.

None of that compares to the littany of accidents that befall stunt performers who don’t even got nominated for Oscars for their work! These are some of the most terrifying sequences I have ever seen. People falling off of buildings, thrown through glass windows, losing arms. It’s a truly harrowing job that deserves more recognition. Though that day may never come.

snippet.title: Knock at the Cabin Behind the Scenes
snippet.description:
We’re diving deep behind the scenes into M. Night Shyamalan’s new horror movie, “Knock at the Cabin.” Starring Rupert Grint, Dave Bautista, Jonathan Groff, Ben Aldridge, and Kristen Cui, this movie represents itself as a stellar, contained ensemble piece. You might have noticed that all the scenes shot in the cabin were like one long, drawn-out shot. They also used not one, but two cabins from the movie that were built completely from scratch. One was built on location in New Jersey and the other was built in a warehouse so they could control all the technical and visual elements. One of the craziest things we found out was that the actors used real weapons during their fight scenes. The only time they would switch to prop weapons were when it involved swinging at somebody’s head. Can you imagine that being part of your regular 9 to 5 work day? Now, we know Dave Bautista does a fantastic job in his role of Leonard, but it was his most challenging role to date. Because he’s an ex-wrestler he usually gets typecast as an action-hero type character who doesn’t speak much. He said he spoke more in this movie than he has in his entire career! It’s the role he’s been waiting for so he could prove himself as a serious actor. snippet.title: Avatar 1 vs Avatar 2 MAJOR Differences

Let’s face it - the Avatar films will just keep on getting better and better - and just push the boundaries of film making every time. Even with the small step from Avatar 1 to Avatar 2 - produced a ton of differences between each film.
How they managed to pull off filming three movies at the same time - is beyond us. It will soon always be known as someone pulling a James Cameron honestly. While filming multiple movies at once is great - it still adds on a ton more resources needed to get the job done - and the job done right of course. Unlike the first installment - they had a whole lot more of everything for this movie - and most apparently - filmed it underwater. It must’ve been strange for the actors to have been filming on land and then completely underwater for the second one. Really couldn’t have been done without the help of a generous lump sum for Cameron though. A big budget can sometimes make a project turn out better - but Cameron wasn’t just focusing on making Avatar better. He was also actually improving the way films are shot.
We still could never understand how James has any hair left after filming one Avatar movie - let alone a whole series of them! But it seems like whatever he’s got brewing in the writers room is sufficient enough to make the studios budget back and more. What do you think will be different in Avatar 3 if any? Honestly - that maybe something you can’t answer since the team really pulled no punches on this one.

snippet.title: Netflix's KALEIDESCOPE Behind the Making
snippet.description:
How many ways have you watched the show Kaleidoscope!? The inventive series is actually loosely based on a true story. Having a hurricane be a major part of a show made for some very damp days on set - there were actually giant structures FULL of water on the Netflix soundstage. Many of the actors had to film while they were in waist-high water, and anyone who has been on a set knows that filming days are VERY long. Filming this was complicated, which meant a ton of extensive prep and planning had to be done so they could safely and efficiently execute what needed to happen! One of the actors, Giancarlo Esposito, actually performed a ton of his own stunts - and he made it happen underwater because of speakers that were used to help communicate with him!
The series can be watched in any order and still make sense, but just because it worked for us doesn’t mean it made sense for the actors, who would sometimes get totally lost in the story, unsure of where exactly they were in it while shooting! Considering jsut how intense and complex the script process was, it’s no surprise there were a whopping ten different people in the writing room! The jobs of production designers and creative team members were way more involved with this series, but many of them actually really embraced it and were excited to figure out how they could best help tell the story - and they absolutely didn’t disappoint.
